Also carries a hard length limit worth knowing: "Vehicles longer than 20 feet and trailers longer than 12 feet are prohibited beyond Carr Canyon Picnic Area" — that is a truck-only road even without the closure.
offroad.source: USFS Coronado National Forest — Carr Canyon Road #368 Scenic Drive

offroad.name: Montezuma Pass via FR 48 and Border Road #61
offroad.difficulty: not published — Coronado NF describes the route but gives no surface grade or vehicle requirement for the FR 48 / FR 61 dirt sections
offroad.season: Coronado NF lists the route as available year-round.
offroad.note: Paved AZ-83 south from Sonoita to Parker Canyon Lake, then FR 48 and FR 61 angling toward the Huachucas and up to Montezuma Pass at the south end of the range, above Coronado National Memorial. The plateau it crosses sits at about 5,000 ft. FR 61 is the Border Road and runs along the international line — expect Border Patrol traffic and checkpoints.
offroad.source: USFS Coronado National Forest — Arizona Highway #83 to Montezuma Pass Scenic Drive

offroad.name: Box Canyon Road #62
offroad.difficulty: Coronado NF describes an "all-weather gravel road" that "turns to dirt"; no vehicle requirement published
offroad.season: Coronado NF lists it as available year-round.
offroad.note: East off the Madera Canyon road, through Box Canyon under the west face of the Santa Ritas, and out to AZ-83 a few miles north of Sonoita — so it can be driven as the way in or the way out of this stop rather than as a there-and-back. The all-weather designation on the first part is the useful bit: this is the route that still works after rain.
offroad.source: USFS Coronado National Forest — Box Canyon Road (FR 62) Scenic Drive

offroad.name: Ruby Road #289/39
offroad.difficulty: not published by Coronado NF — the page gives no mileage, surface or vehicle requirement, only the route
offroad.season: No gate published.
offroad.note: West off I-19 north of Nogales at the Ruby interchange, paved to Peña Blanca Lake where it becomes FR 39, then dirt through grass savanna and past the Ruby ghost town toward Arivaca. Sycamore Canyon and Arivaca Lake are on it. Furthest afield of this stop's three and the one to give a full day.
offroad.source: USFS Coronado National Forest — Ruby Road #289/39 Scenic Drive

offroad.name: Canelo Hills Loops #799/58/49
offroad.difficulty: not published — Coronado NF gives the route and the country but no length, surface or vehicle requirement
offroad.season: Coronado NF lists the route status as open; no gate published.
offroad.note: Off AZ-83 south of Sonoita onto FR 5799 and through the Canelo Hills — "historic ranching and mining country with broad grasslands and distant buttes" — ending in Patagonia. Loops back to the stop itself, which is what makes it the easy pick of the three. Neither restrooms nor water anywhere on it.
offroad.source: USFS Coronado National Forest — Canelo Hills Loops #799/58/49 Scenic Drive

offroad.name: Apache Trail (SR 88) unpaved section
offroad.distance: the unpaved section runs from Fish Creek Vista (milepost 222) to milepost 227 near Reavis Trailhead Road
offroad.difficulty: not graded. ADOT describes the 1.5-mile section at Fish Creek Vista as "steep and more winding and narrow than other parts of SR 88" and asks drivers to ensure vehicles are "appropriate for unpaved terrain"
offroad.season: Open, and that is not a given — this section was closed from 2019 and reopened in stages; monsoon damage shut it again in 2026 and it was repaired and reopened that July. ADOT: "Although there are currently no vehicle restrictions," the status "can change should severe weather or rockfall affect conditions." Check the ADOT project page before driving out.
offroad.note: Approach it from the Globe end via Roosevelt Dam rather than from Apache Junction — the stop sits at the far end of the Trail from the tourist traffic. Fish Creek Hill is the famous bit and the reason to go. The most-changed road on this whole itinerary; verify status the week before.
offroad.source: Arizona Department of Transportation — SR 88 Apache Trail project page

offroad.name: Pinal Peak via Forest Road 651
offroad.difficulty: described as "washboarded dirt that's deeply rutted in places"; no Forest Service grade found
offroad.season: NOT VERIFIED, and this matters. Pinal Peak tops out near 7,800 ft directly above Globe, and secondary sources describe the road as a May-September proposition. The stop is 2-4 Mar 2028. No Tonto National Forest page publishing a gate date for FR 651 was found — treat access as unverified rather than assured, and phone the Globe Ranger District. Do not assume it is open because the desert below is warm.
offroad.note: Straight up out of Globe into ponderosa — an 8,000 ft climb-out from a Sonoran-desert town in a single afternoon, which is the appeal. Pinal Campground is on the way up. Recorded from Arizona Highways because no Forest Service page describing this road was found; the mileage and any restriction are unsourced.
offroad.source: Arizona Highways — Pinal Peak

offroad.name: Forest Road 302 to Grandview Lookout Tower (Coconino Rim Road / FR 310)
offroad.distance: about 16.9 miles from the Tusayan Ranger District — FR 302 for approximately 15 miles, then FR 310 for approximately 1.4 miles. From inside the park it is about 18 miles: US-64 east, then "Coconino Rim Road/Forest Road 310 and follow for approximately 1.3 miles"
offroad.difficulty: NOT PUBLISHED. Kaibab National Forest gives the route and the mileages and says nothing about surface, high clearance or 4WD — recorded as unknown rather than guessed.
offroad.season: No gate date published. About 7,000 ft on the Coconino Rim and the stop arrives 12 Mar 2028, so late-season snow and spring mud are both live. The Forest publishes no winter status for these roads.
offroad.note: The straightforward version of the Grandview country: graded forest road from Tusayan out to the 1936 Grandview Lookout Tower, with a paved return into the park on SR 64 if the dirt turns bad. FR 310 leaves Desert View Drive within minutes of the park boundary. This is the answer to "where can the truck go off pavement at the South Rim" — because inside Grand Canyon National Park it cannot; the park has no unpaved road open to visitor driving on this rim, and Tuweep's rough roads are on the far side of the canyon, a five-hour drive, not a day trip.
offroad.source: USFS Kaibab National Forest — Vishnu Trail #125 (driving directions)

offroad.name: Grandview Loop — Forest Roads 302, 310, 2718 and 2719
offroad.distance: 30.4-mile loop — FR 302 for 14.3 miles east from Tusayan, FR 310 (Coconino Rim Road) for 2.1, FR 2718 for 1.5, FR 2719 for 6, then FR 302 for 6.5 back
offroad.difficulty: "A high-clearance vehicle is required for forest roads 2718 and 2719, and four-wheel-drive is recommended." FR 302 and 310 are ordinary graded forest road.
offroad.season: No published gate. This is Kaibab NF at about 7,000 ft on the Coconino Rim and the stop arrives 12 Mar 2028 — late-season snow and spring mud are both live possibilities on FR 2718/2719. The paved bail-out is stated on the source: passenger cars can enter the park and return on SR 64 instead.
offroad.note: This is the answer to "where can the truck actually go off pavement at the South Rim", because inside the park it cannot. Kaibab National Forest wraps the park's south boundary and FR 310 (Coconino Rim Road) leaves Desert View Drive within minutes of the park line, running to the 1936 Grandview Lookout Tower. Recorded from Arizona Highways — the Kaibab NF pages found do not describe this route.
offroad.source: Arizona Highways — Grandview Loop

offroad.name: Smithsonian Butte National Back Country Byway
offroad.distance: 9.25 miles
offroad.difficulty: BLM publishes no surface grade or vehicle requirement for it — an absence worth knowing, since the byway designation makes it sound easier than the warning below implies
offroad.season: BLM: "This route often becomes impassable during heavy rain and periods of inclement winter weather." The stop is 15-21 Mar 2028 — late enough that winter weather is unlikely but spring rain is not. No gate; the surface is the gate.
offroad.note: The stop's own road. It runs between Rockville and Apple Valley, just south of Zion and a couple of miles from the Virgin base, climbing to the mesa top under Smithsonian Butte with the Zion cliffs behind. "No services are available along the Byway." The Grafton ghost town road branches off the Rockville end.
offroad.source: BLM Utah — Smithsonian Butte National Back Country Byway

offroad.name: Gooseberry Mesa Road
offroad.difficulty: not published as a driving grade. BLM's mesa map is written for mountain bikers — "Slickrock portions of trail are marked with white dots" — and it is the authority on which routes are open to vehicles, so read it before driving anything beyond the main mesa road
offroad.season: No gate published. Same wet-weather caveat as Smithsonian Butte; the mesa clay is the problem.
offroad.note: The mesa immediately south of Smithsonian Butte, reached off the byway, with a rim view straight into Zion. Included with a caution: the published material here is bike material, and BLM's map — not a trail database — decides which routes a vehicle may use.
offroad.source: BLM Utah — Gooseberry Mesa map (PDF)

offroad.name: Cottonwood Canyons Scenic Backway
offroad.distance: 46 miles from Cannonville south to US-89 — "paved for 9 miles between Cannonville and the turnoff to Kodachrome Basin State Park", dirt for the remaining 37
offroad.difficulty: BLM publishes no vehicle requirement for it
offroad.season: No calendar gate — the surface is the gate. This is bentonite clay: fine when dry, undriveable within minutes of rain, and late March is not a dry month. BLM publishes a road condition report for Grand Staircase-Escalante, "typically updated weekly, more frequently if road conditions warrant", at https://www.blm.gov/documents/utah/public-room/data/road-report — read it the morning of, not the week before.
offroad.note: The big day out from Bryce and one of the best dirt roads in southern Utah, running the length of the Cockscomb through Grand Staircase-Escalante. Cannonville is about 15 miles from the stop, so the road starts almost at the door. Kodachrome Basin State Park is on the paved part.
offroad.source: BLM Utah — Cottonwood Canyons Scenic Backway

offroad.name: Skutumpah Road
offroad.difficulty: described as a "rough, washboarded dirt road" whose conditions "can change from day to day depending on weather, maintenance" — that wording is from AllTrails, not from BLM; BLM's own report gives status rather than a grade
offroad.season: Same as Cottonwood Canyon and for the same reason. No calendar closure; BLM's weekly road report is the source that actually answers the question on the day.
offroad.note: The other road out of Cannonville, running southwest across the Skutumpah Terrace toward Johnson Canyon and Kanab, past the Willis Creek and Bull Valley Gorge slot trailheads. Pairs naturally with Cottonwood Canyon Road — one out, one back — but that is a long day and both need to be dry.
offroad.source: BLM Utah — Grand Staircase-Escalante road condition report (description from AllTrails)

offroad.name: North Rim Road
offroad.distance: NPS publishes no length, only that "The last 7 miles of the park access road and the entire North Rim Drive road are unpaved gravel"
offroad.difficulty: not graded by NPS; no vehicle requirement or length limit published
offroad.season: LIKELY CONFLICTS WITH THE STOP DATES. NPS: "The North Rim is closed to vehicles in the winter and early spring" and "In winter and early spring, these roads are unplowed and the North Rim is closed to vehicles." The stop is 8-10 Apr 2028 — squarely in what NPS calls early spring. No exact opening date is published, which makes this a phone call rather than a plan.
offroad.note: The quiet rim. Gravel the whole way in, five overlooks reachable by car, and a fraction of the South Rim's traffic. Reached from CO-92: "turn west on Black Canyon Road approximately 3 miles south of Crawford" — which from a South Rim base is a long way round the canyon, roughly two hours. If it is open on these dates it is the best thing at this stop; if it is gated, the stop has essentially no unpaved driving.
offroad.source: NPS Black Canyon of the Gunnison — North Rim

offroad.name: East Portal Road
offroad.difficulty: paved, but a "winding, steep road down the canyon" at a 16% grade with tight curves; vehicles longer than 22 feet are prohibited
offroad.season: Closes seasonally for winter; the stop's 8-10 Apr 2028 dates sit near the reopening, and there is a further complication — the road was closed after the July 2025 South Rim Fire because of unstable slopes. Check https://www.nps.gov/blca/planyourvisit/conditions.htm before counting on it.
offroad.note: Not dirt, so it is only half an offroad entry — but it is the only way to drive to the river inside the park, it drops 2,000 ft in a couple of miles, and the 22 ft limit makes it a truck-only trip in exactly the way the dirt roads are. Included for that reason, flagged for what it is.
offroad.source: NPS Black Canyon of the Gunnison — East Portal

offroad.name: La Plata Canyon Road (FR 124) toward Kennebec Pass
offroad.distance: about 15 miles from Hesperus up the canyon, climbing nearly 3,000 ft toward Kennebec Pass at 11,683 ft
offroad.difficulty: graded gravel low down; 4WD with good clearance for the last section to the pass. The mileage and the 4WD note are from theridrs.com and dangerousroads.org, not from the Forest — San Juan NF publishes the gate status but not a grade.
offroad.season: Partly open, and the distinction is the whole answer. San Juan NF's road table lists FR 124 as "Open", with the gate closing "12/15 or 4 inches standing at the gate" — so the lower canyon should be driveable on the stop's 15-22 Apr 2028 dates. The top will not be: Kennebec Pass is above 11,600 ft and holds snow well into summer. Drive it as far as it goes, not as a pass crossing.
offroad.note: The best dirt within reach of a Mesa Verde base, and it is not at Mesa Verde — the park's own roads are all paved and the park prohibits leaving them. La Plata Canyon is old mining country north of Hesperus, about 45 minutes east of Mancos.
offroad.source: USFS San Juan National Forest — Current Conditions road table

offroad.name: Bolam Pass Road (FR 578)
offroad.difficulty: not graded on the Forest's table
offroad.season: CONFLICTS WITH THE STOP DATES. San Juan NF gives FR 578 an opening date of "5/1" and closing dates "9/8-10/13, 11/30". The stop is 15-22 Apr 2028 — the gate opens nine days after departure. This one is simply not available on these dates.
offroad.note: The high crossing between Durango and Rico via Hermosa Park, and the reason it is listed rather than dropped is that it is the obvious thing to want at this stop and it is shut. Recorded so the card says what is being missed and why. Anything at that elevation in the San Juans is a July proposition, not an April one.
offroad.source: USFS San Juan National Forest — Current Conditions road table

offroad.name: Canyons of the Ancients — Lowry Pueblo and Painted Hand Pueblo roads
offroad.difficulty: not graded by BLM. A secondary description of the drive: "trips takes you from a paved road to a dirt road which is sometimes primitive. Most vehicles with good clearance will be fine."
offroad.season: No gate published. Mid-April is a good time for it — low country west of Cortez at around 6,000 ft, clear of snow, and the clay dries fast. Wet-weather caveat applies to the primitive sections.
offroad.note: The low-elevation alternative for a stop whose mountain roads are still gated. Over 6,000 recorded sites; Lowry Pueblo has a stabilised great kiva and Painted Hand is the one that needs the dirt. Roughly 40 minutes northwest of Cortez. Mesa Verde itself contributes nothing here — every road in that park is paved and driving off them is prohibited.
offroad.source: BLM — Canyons of the Ancients National Monument

offroad.name: Piedra Road (FR 631)
offroad.difficulty: not graded on the Forest's table
offroad.season: OPEN, and unusually so for this stop. San Juan NF's road table says FR 631 "Remains open all year, plowed in winter" — it is one of very few roads in the district that is. The stop is 27-30 Apr 2028, when almost everything else at altitude is still behind a 5/1 or 6/1 gate.
offroad.note: The main road north out of Pagosa Springs into the Piedra country and toward the Weminuche — and, on these dates, effectively the only high-country road out of this stop that can be counted on. Williams Creek is off it and is also listed as open all year and plowed.
offroad.source: USFS San Juan National Forest — Current Conditions road table

offroad.name: Buckles Lake Road
offroad.difficulty: not graded on the Forest's table
offroad.season: UNCERTAIN ON THESE DATES. San Juan NF lists its opening as "Conditional" with a 1/15 closure — meaning there is no fixed spring date and the Forest opens it when the road can take traffic. Late April in the eastern San Juans is early for that. Phone the Pagosa Ranger District rather than driving out on spec.
offroad.note: Southeast of Pagosa toward the Continental Divide and the New Mexico line. Listed with its 'conditional' status stated plainly rather than omitted, because 'conditional' is the actual answer and a card that said nothing would read as 'open'. The broader picture for this stop: most San Juan NF gates open 5/1 or 6/1, one to five weeks after departure.
offroad.source: USFS San Juan National Forest — Current Conditions road table
